nodes.text: Chapter 20: Current, Resistance, Ohm’s Law, Power, AC/DC

nodes.detailed_figure_description: Hand-drawn simple circuit consisting of a battery on the left connected by a rectangular wire loop. The battery’s upper terminal is marked positive and its lower terminal negative; an orange V labels the voltage. Blue arrows marked I show conventional current moving clockwise around the loop. Black arrows and e⁻ labels show electrons moving in the opposite direction, counterclockwise, including downward through the battery.
nodes.figure_alternative: Diagram of a battery circuit contrasting clockwise conventional current with counterclockwise electron flow.

nodes.text: Electrical current (I) is the rate of flow of positive charge.

nodes.spoken_math_alternative: I equals Q divided by delta t, which equals Q divided by t.

nodes.text: It’s direction (from DC, or direct current, voltage) is opposite the “flow” of electrons: from + to −.

nodes.spoken_math_alternative: The unit of amperes equals coulombs per second.

nodes.text: Electric fields in a Simple Circuit (1962)

nodes.detailed_figure_description: Annotated grayscale photograph of a simple circuit or conductor arrangement with two leads entering from above and curved field patterns visible around and within the conductor. A left callout points into the conductor and reads, “Internal electric field: constant magnitude and parallel to the axis of the conductor.” A right callout points outside it and reads, “External electric field: Produced by the surface charges.”
nodes.figure_alternative: Annotated photograph comparing the internal electric field along a conductor with the external electric field produced by surface charges.

warnings.message: The handwritten “It’s direction” appears to use the contraction “It’s” where the possessive “Its” was likely intended; the source wording has been preserved.
